description: Canonical ONNX operator support database for SiMa MLA.

Add.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Same shape, or exactly one input is a scalar, or both inputs are broadcastable
Add.notes: Can be fused with conv or matmul.

ArgMax.attributes:
axis = [-r, r-1]
keepdim = [1, 0]
select_last_index = [0, 1]

output int64
ArgMax.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
Output is int32 (HW has no int64)
axis = channel axis only (SW)
ArgMax.notes:
1. Keepdim=False can be supported (for 2D spatial and above)
2. Reduce on spatial dimensions can be supported.
3. There is no int64 in HW.
4. Compiler supports multiple batches.
Channel axis is inferred by layout analysis.

AveragePool.attributes:
auto_pad = [NOTSET, SAME_UPPER, SAME_LOWER or VALID]
ceil_mode = [0, 1]
count_include_pad = [0, 1]
kernel_shape
pads
strides
AveragePool.tvm_transforms_constraints: auto_pad is converted to explicit pad.
AveragePool.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
count_include_pad = 1 (HW)
kernel_shape: If global pool, no size limit; otherwise size < 128. (HW. Workaround by SW)
dilations = 1 for newer opset (HW)
AveragePool.notes:
1. If global pool, any shape.
2. The 128 is from the HW instruction limit in gen1 and gen2. Possible to impove in compiler.
3. Possible to improve compiler to support any shape.
4. HW does not support count_include_pad=False. Possible to support in compiler or Model Compiler.
5. ceil_mode=True is handled by the rewrite rule SetCeilModeToFalseForNDPooling.
6. dilation>1 is not supported by HW.

Expand.tvm_transforms_constraints: Lowered to BroadcastToOp after constant folding the requested shape.
Expand.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Shape must be compile-time constant and broadcast-compatible. Batch dimension cannot be broadcast or changed. (SW)
Expand.business_study: Dynamic shape input or batch broadcasting
Expand.notes: ONNX Expand is the canonical source operator; BroadcastToOp is the internal AFE lowering.

Conv.attributes:
auto_pad = [NOTSET, SAME_UPPER, SAME_LOWER or VALID]
dilations
group
kernel_shape
pads
strides
Conv.tvm_transforms_constraints: auto_pad is converted to explicit pad.
Conv.notes: fused with bias and activation.  ONNX does not have 1D convolution, though we support it for other frontends.

ConvTranspose.attributes:
auto_pad = [NOTSET, SAME_UPPER, SAME_LOWER or VALID]
dilations
group
kernel_shape
output_padding
output_shape
pads
strides
ConvTranspose.tvm_transforms_constraints: auto_pad is converted to explicit pad.
ConvTranspose.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
dilations == 1 (HW)
group = 1 (HW) or depthwise (SW)
stride =  [1, 2, 4, 8, 16] non-depthwise; [1, 2] depthwise (SW)
ConvTranspose.business_study:
dilations > 1
group > 1
strides = not power of 2
ConvTranspose.notes:
fused with bias and activation.
1. If depthwise, possible to support stride of power of 2.
Other group size could be supported by splitting into multiple operations.
ONNX does not have 1D conv_transpose.  It would be possible to support 1D by converting to 2D.

Cos.sima_hw_sw_constraints: INT8 activation only. A bfloat16 activation request inserts casts and executes Cos as an INT8 lookup-table UDF.
Cos.notes: Ranks 1 through 5 were verified on MLA with automatic layout conversion. INT8 lookup-table accuracy depends on representative calibration data covering the deployed input range.

CumSum.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
reverse = 0 (SW)
Size <= 257 on summation axis. (SW)
Must have exactly one summation axis. (SW)
Axis must be a constant. (HW)
CumSum.notes:
Converted to Conv2d.  Larger size or reverse=1 can be handled.
Automatic layout conversion handles any number of non-summation dimensions.

Div.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Same shape, or exactly one input is a scalar, or both inputs are broadcastable

Einsum.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
Must have two input tensors. (SW)
Supports any equation where each variable is used in at least two tensors and at most once in each tensor.  An example violating the first condition is jk,k->k (j is not used in at least two tensors).  An example violating the second condition is jk,kk->j (k is used twice in one tensor). (SW)
Einsum.notes:
Converted to batch matmul.
The kernel supports equations "nhwc,nhqc->nhwq" and "nhwc,nhcq->nhwq".  Other equations are handled by layout conversion.

Gather.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Indices must be a constant, and it must be 0D or 1D. (HW)

Gemm.attributes:
alpha: float
beta: float
transA = [0, 1]
transB = [0, 1]
optional C input
Gemm.tvm_transforms_constraints: Imported as dense and lowered to an MLA convolution. B must be a compile-time constant initializer.
Gemm.sima_hw_sw_constraints: A and B must be rank-2. B must be a compile-time constant initializer; a runtime B input is unsupported and fails before backend partitioning. alpha and beta may be finite floating-point values. transB = 0 or 1 is supported. transA = 1 requires flexible_batch_size=False because the leading dimension of A is K rather than batch. Optional constant C supports scalar, [N], [1,N], or [M,N]; constant [M,1] is unsupported. A runtime C remains entirely on MLA only for [1,N], [M,1], or [M,N]; runtime scalar or [N] C uses APU fallback.
Gemm.business_study: Runtime B input; constant C with [M,1] shape; runtime scalar or [N] C without fallback
Gemm.notes: Verified with all transA/transB combinations and representative alpha/beta values 0, 1, 0.5, and -1. Both bfloat16 activations with INT8 weights and bfloat16 activations with bfloat16 weights map to MLA. With the default flexible-batch workflow, transA = 0 treats M as batch; disable flexible batching for general fixed-M GEMM or transA = 1.

GlobalAveragePool.tvm_transforms_constraints: Lowered to global average pooling on MLA.
GlobalAveragePool.notes: Global pooling has no kernel-size limit.

GlobalMaxPool.tvm_transforms_constraints: Lowered to global max pooling on MLA.
GlobalMaxPool.notes: Global pooling has no kernel-size limit.

GridSample.attributes:
align_corners = [0, 1]
mode = [bilinear, nearest, bicubic]
padding_mode = [zeros, border, reflection]
NCHW only
GridSample.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
Limited kernel for RaftStereo: sampling on W axis only. (SW)
mode = 'linear'
padding_mode != 'reflection'
GridSample.notes: The compiler support for this is not standard and is only specific to the requirement of raft stereo(?). If needed, we need to revisit the kernel and determine how to implement it.

HardSwish.notes: Same as HardSigmoidwith alpha = 1/6 and beta = 0.5

InstanceNormalization.notes: Possible to support any shape in compiler

LayerNormalization.attributes:
axis: first norm axis
epsilon
stash_type: [1, 10]
LayerNormalization.notes:
Second stage of scale and shift are converted to conv2d.
Possible to support any shape in compiler. Currently only support 1/2/3D.
Automatic layout conversion transforms it to the appropriate axis.

LRN.notes: Possible to support any shape in compiler

MeanVarianceNormalization.attributes: axes: list of reduction axes; default = [0, 2, 3]
MeanVarianceNormalization.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed into mean, subtract, multiply, sqrt/rsqrt, and divide operations.
MeanVarianceNormalization.sima_hw_sw_constraints: INT8 activation only. A bfloat16 activation request inserts casts, but sqrt/rsqrt and some reduction paths still execute as INT8. Rank-5 (3D spatial) axis handling is layout-pattern dependent and is not generally supported; use rank 4 or lower for portable MLA support. The selected axes must produce nonzero variance because this ONNX operator has no epsilon attribute.
MeanVarianceNormalization.business_study: Native bfloat16 activation support; general rank-5 axis support
MeanVarianceNormalization.notes: All non-empty rank-4 axis combinations were mapped to MLA. Reduction over only a singleton dimension produces zero variance and fails calibration mathematically. The default axes [0,2,3] are supported.

MaxPool.attributes:
auto_pad = [NOTSET, SAME_UPPER, SAME_LOWER or VALID]
ceil_mode = [0, 1]
dilations
kernel_shape
pads
storage_order = [0, 1]
strides

Optional indices output
MaxPool.tvm_transforms_constraints: auto_pad is converted to explicit pad.
MaxPool.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
dilations = 1 (HW)
kernel_shape: If global pool, no size limit; otherwise size < 128. (HW)

storage_order: No optional indices tensor output (SW)
MaxPool.notes:
1. If global pool, any shape.
2. The 128 is from the HW instruction limit in gen1 and gen2. Possible to impove in compiler.
3. Possible to improve compiler to support any shape.
4.  ceil_mode=True is handled by the rewrite rule SetCeilModeToFalseForNDPooling.
5. dilation>1 is not supported by HW.

Mul.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Same shape, or exactly one input is a scalar, or both inputs are broadcastable

Pad.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
mode: only ‘constant’ mode with value 0. (SW)
At most 2 dimensions may have a nonzero padding width. (SW)
Pad.notes:
Converted to average pool.
1. Possible to support other constant values in Model Compiler.
2. Pad in channel dimension can be supported in Model Compiler.
3. Other padding modes do not have HW support but can be supported in compiler.

Pow.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Input exponent is scalar constant 0.5, -0.5, 2, or 3. (SW)
Pow.notes:
1. Not sure what's the reason why constant can only be 2 or 3. Not sure why it cannot be supported using LUT.
2. With FP input and exponent, possible to support in compiler.

ReduceL2.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Expect following DIV to merge to L2 normalization.

ReduceMean.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
For 1D reduce, axis is spatial dimension only. (SW)
If all spatial axes, no size limit; otherwise, size in spatial axes less than 128. (HW)
ReduceMean.notes: Spatial+channel is decomposed into 2 operations.  Channel reduction is converted to conv2d or conv3d.  Spatial and channel axes are inferred by layout analysis.

ReduceSum.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
For 1D reduce, axis is spatial dimension only. (SW)
If all spatial axes, no size limit; otherwise, size in spatial axes less than 128. (SW)
ReduceSum.notes: Spatial+channel is decomposed into 2 operations.  Channel reduction is converted to conv2d or conv3d.  Spatial and channel axes are inferred by layout analysis.

ReduceMin.notes: It is possible to support like ReduceMax.

Reshape.notes: batch_flatten, expand_dims, and squeeze are converted to reshape, and they are supported if the reshape operator is supported

Resize.attributes:
coordinate_transformation_mode = [half_pixel, pytorch_half_pixel, align_corners, asymmetric, tf_crop_and_resize]
cubic_coeff_a: float
exclude_outside = [0, 1]
extrapolation_value: float
mode = [nearest, linear, cubic]
nearest_mode = [round_prefer_floor, round_prefer_ceil, floor, ceil]

1-4 inputs
Resize.sima_hw_sw_constraints:
mode = [nearest, linear] (HW/SW)
coordinate_transformation_mode= 'tf_crop_and_resize' not supported. (SW)
If method is 'linear', any scaling factor is supported. However,
for 8-bit integers any scaling more than 63 may lead to loss in accuracy. (HW)
If the method is 'nearest', then the scaling factor must be a power of two (HW), or the scaling factor must be an even integer (using the same factor in both dimensions) and the coordinate transformation mode must be half_pixel and the rounding mode must be floor. (SW)
Any other method or scaling factor is not supported.

Single input only. (SW)
Resize.business_study:
mode = cubic
ctm = 'tf_crop_and_resize' 
restrictions in nearest mode.
Resize.notes: Some cases are converted to pool2d by DownscaleResizeToPooling.

Sin.sima_hw_sw_constraints: INT8 activation only. A bfloat16 activation request inserts casts and executes Sin as an INT8 lookup-table UDF.
Sin.notes: Ranks 1 through 5 were verified on MLA with automatic layout conversion. INT8 lookup-table accuracy depends on representative calibration data covering the deployed input range.

Sub.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Same shape, or exactly one input is a scalar, or both inputs are broadcastable

Abs.notes: The rewrite is mathematically equivalent to absolute value.

Flatten.sima_hw_sw_constraints: axis = 1 so the batch dimension is preserved. Input and output must be at least 2D. (SW)
Flatten.notes: The default ONNX axis is supported.

GlobalLpPool.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to power, global average pooling, multiply, absolute value, and square root.
GlobalLpPool.sima_hw_sw_constraints: p = 2. Static input shape. Input rank = 3, 4, or 5. (SW)
GlobalLpPool.notes: The square-root stage executes as an INT8 lookup-table UDF in a BF16 model.

LogSoftmax.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to SoftmaxOp followed by LogOp; automatic layout conversion maps the selected axis to the MLA channel axis.
LogSoftmax.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Input and output must be at least 2D. (SW)
LogSoftmax.notes: In a BF16 model, the Log stage executes as an INT8 lookup-table UDF.

LpPool.attributes:
auto_pad
ceil_mode
dilations
kernel_shape
p
pads
strides
LpPool.tvm_transforms_constraints: For p=2, decomposed to multiply, AvgPoolOp, absolute value, scaling, and SqrtOp. auto_pad is converted to explicit padding.
LpPool.sima_hw_sw_constraints: p = 2. dilation = 1. ceil_mode = 0. Static shapes. Kernel size < 128 in every spatial dimension unless the pool is global. (HW/SW)
LpPool.business_study: p != 2, dilation > 1, ceil_mode = 1, dynamic shapes, or kernel size > 127
LpPool.notes: Other values of p leave an unsupported general Power operation. The square-root stage executes in INT8 for a BF16 model.

Mean.tvm_transforms_constraints: Inputs are stacked with ExpandDimsOp and TupleConcatenateOp, then reduced with MeanOp.
Mean.sima_hw_sw_constraints: All inputs have the same shape and batch dimension. Fewer than 128 inputs. (SW/HW)
Mean.business_study: Broadcast inputs or 128 or more inputs
Mean.notes: MeanOp currently computes in INT8 even when BF16 activations are requested.

Mish.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to ExpOp, AddOp, LogOp, TanhOp, and MultiplyOp.
Mish.notes: In a BF16 model, the Log stage executes as an INT8 lookup-table UDF.

Neg.tvm_transforms_constraints: Rewritten to MultiplyOp with the scalar constant -1.

ReduceL1.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to Abs and SumOp; automatic layout conversion preserves the requested output rank.
ReduceL1.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Use ONNX opset <= 17 so axes are an attribute. If reducing a subset of spatial axes, each reduced extent must be < 128; reducing all spatial axes has no size limit. (SW/HW)
ReduceL1.business_study: ONNX opset >= 18 axes input or partial spatial reduction extent > 127
ReduceL1.notes: Channel reduction is decomposed to MLA-supported operations.

ReduceLogSum.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to SumOp followed by LogOp; automatic layout conversion preserves the requested output rank.
ReduceLogSum.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Use ONNX opset <= 17 so axes are an attribute. If reducing a subset of spatial axes, each reduced extent must be < 128; reducing all spatial axes has no size limit. Reduced sums must be in the Log domain. (SW/HW)
ReduceLogSum.business_study: ONNX opset >= 18 axes input, partial spatial reduction extent > 127, or non-positive reduced sum
ReduceLogSum.notes: In a BF16 model, the Log stage executes as an INT8 lookup-table UDF.

ReduceLogSumExp.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed into MLA reduction and elementwise/UDF operations; automatic layout conversion preserves the requested output rank.
ReduceLogSumExp.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Use ONNX opset <= 17 so axes are an attribute. If reducing a subset of spatial axes, each reduced extent must be < 128; reducing all spatial axes has no size limit. (SW/HW)
ReduceLogSumExp.business_study: ONNX opset >= 18 axes input or partial spatial reduction extent > 127
ReduceLogSumExp.notes: In a BF16 model, the Log stage executes as an INT8 lookup-table UDF.

ReduceSumSquare.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to MultiplyOp followed by SumOp; automatic layout conversion preserves the requested output rank.
ReduceSumSquare.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Use ONNX opset <= 17 so axes are an attribute. If reducing a subset of spatial axes, each reduced extent must be < 128; reducing all spatial axes has no size limit. (SW/HW)
ReduceSumSquare.business_study: ONNX opset >= 18 axes input or partial spatial reduction extent > 127
ReduceSumSquare.notes: Channel reduction is decomposed to MLA-supported operations.

Softsign.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to Abs, AddOp, and DivideOp.

Squeeze.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Axes input must be compile-time constant, may select only dimensions of size 1, and cannot remove the batch axis. Output must be at least 2D. (SW)
Squeeze.business_study: Dynamic axes, batch-axis removal, or scalar/1D output

Sum.tvm_transforms_constraints: Lowered to a chain of AddOps.
Sum.sima_hw_sw_constraints: All inputs have the same rank and batch dimension. Other dimensions are equal or 1. (SW)

Tile.tvm_transforms_constraints: Decomposed to ReshapeOp and TupleConcatenateOp operations.
Tile.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Repeats must be compile-time constant and the batch-axis repeat must be 1. Input and output must be at least 2D. (SW)

TopK.attributes:
axis = [-r, r-1]
largest = [0, 1]
sorted = [0, 1]
K: constant input
TopK.tvm_transforms_constraints: The two ONNX outputs are split into separate MLA TopKOp operations. Automatic layout conversion maps the selected axis to channel.
TopK.sima_hw_sw_constraints: K must be compile-time constant, 1 <= K < selected-axis size, and largest = 1. Input and outputs must be at least 2D. ONNX int64 indices are emitted as int32 because MLA has no int64. (SW/HW)
TopK.business_study: Dynamic K, K >= axis size, largest = 0, scalar/1D tensors, or int64 indices
TopK.notes: Both values and indices are supported after SplitTopK; sorted=0 may still produce sorted output, which satisfies the ONNX unordered-output contract.

Unsqueeze.sima_hw_sw_constraints: Axes input must be compile-time constant and cannot insert a new batch axis. Input and output must be at least 2D. (SW)
Unsqueeze.business_study: Dynamic axes, new batch axis, or scalar/1D tensors
